title: Introducing automatic remediation policies with Cloudflare CASB
partialText: Cloudflare CASB policies introduce a native automation engine built directly on the Cloudflare developer platform to remediate SaaS risks automatically. Security teams can now design event-driven logic to revoke risky file shares and send webhooks without manual intervention.

title: 1.1.1.1 now supports post-quantum DNSSEC, all 2,420 bytes of it
partialText: 1.1.1.1 now validates DNSSEC signatures using NIST’s post-quantum ML-DSA-44 algorithm. Here is how we manage 2,420-byte signatures and downgrade risks at scale.

title: How we rebuilt Cloudflare Workers’ module registry for Node.js compatibility
partialText: Workers now enables Node.js compatibility by default, supports applications up to 64 mebibytes, and adds a URL-based module registry with import.meta, lazy compilation, shared code caches, and clearer errors.

title: Automatic Key Exchange: faster, post-quantum secure origin handshakes for 45 billion daily connections (and counting)
partialText: Automatic Key Exchange probes TLS 1.3-capable customer origins to learn which key agreement algorithms they support. We then lead with the most secure algorithm when connecting to the origin, preferring post-quantum connections wherever the origin supports it.

title: Introducing context-aware vulnerability discovery and remediation with Cloudflare Managed Defense and OpenAI Daybreak models
partialText: Use production traffic and security signals to prioritize findings, prepare edge mitigations when safe, and propose code patches. By combining WAF data with OpenAI Daybreak models, Vulnerability Discovery and Remediation helps teams identify and patch the most critical threats first.

title: How we could save petabytes of cache storage with Zstandard and Pingora
partialText: Could we get more cache space with the same hardware? We prototyped compression inside Cloudflare's cache to find out.

title: Introducing Adaptive Intelligence: Undermining the economics of every bot attack
partialText: Bot operators have historically had the economic advantage, bypassing static, deterministic detection rules with cheap proxies and retooling. Cloudflare's new Adaptive Intelligence engine flips this dynamic by autonomously learning from the meta-signals of live traffic and deploying disposable rules, making automated attacks too expensive to sustain.

title: BotBase for Operators: A clearer path to joining Cloudflare's directory of bots and agents
partialText: Bot operators now have a home in the Cloudflare dashboard to manage submissions. This update adds submission status tracking, submission editing, and a behavior model so operators can accurately declare how their bots use content.

title: How we saved 100 terabytes of memory by optimizing 1.1.1.1’s DNS cache
partialText: Five Rust-level memory optimizations to the DNS cache layout of Big Pineapple cut per-entry memory by 56%, freeing approximately 100 TB of memory across Cloudflare's fleet.

title: The Cloudflare Blog — brought to you by EmDash
partialText: We migrated the Cloudflare Blog to EmDash to prove our stack at massive scale. Here is how we stress-tested performance, safely routed production traffic, and redesigned the frontend experience.

title: Say it once: Introducing Bot Preference Sync
partialText: Cloudflare's new Bot Preference Sync automatically aligns your robots.txt file with your AI bot policies for Search, Agent, and Training. Easily manage which bots access your content without maintaining static files.

title: From all-or-nothing to task-based OAuth consent
partialText: Cloudflare OAuth now supports optional scopes, giving users more control over what an app can access and helping developers build secure consent flows around the task at hand.

title: A revisit of remote Spectre attacks on Cloudflare Workers
partialText: In 2024 and 2025, we reassessed remote Spectre attacks on our Workers infrastructure. We share details about the new attack primitives like Spectre gadgets, remote timers, achieving co-location  and how new defenses further harden Cloudflare Workers.

title: BGP Role model: tracking the adoption of RFC 9234
partialText: RFC 9234 lets routers reject route leaks on their own, using BGP Roles and the Only to Customer attribute. We measured who has deployed it, and found two Tier 1 networks unexpectedly stripping OTC.

title: How Cloudflare detects MCP traffic and helps secure it
partialText: Cloudflare Gateway identifies MCP requests using protocol-level heuristics. Security teams can use that signal to find shadow MCP traffic, enforce Portal-only access for approved servers, and block direct connections on managed network paths.

title: Secure all your internal vibe-coded applications — in one click
partialText: Introducing Cloudflare Access for Workers. Attach an Access policy directly to a Worker and it applies everywhere that Worker runs — routes, custom domains, workers.dev, and previews — automatically.

title: Total eclipse of the Internet: traffic impacts in Iceland, Spain, and Portugal
partialText: Cloudflare's data shows a clear impact on Internet traffic from Iceland to Spain and Portugal, following the path of totality of the total solar eclipse that occurred on August 12, 2026.

title: Certificate Transparency Monitoring is now generally available
partialText: Cloudflare's Certificate Transparency Monitoring is now generally available. The biggest change: we no longer email you about certificates Cloudflare issued for your domain, so when an alert lands in your inbox, it's worth a look.

title: Cloudflare DDoS Threat Report H1 2026: 1 Tbps attacks soar as DNS floods and geopolitical tensions drive a new wave
partialText: In the first half of 2026, Cloudflare detected a 519% surge in hyper-volumetric DDos attacks across its network.  These attacks were driven heavily by DNS and CLDAP reflection vectors. This report breaks down how major geopolitical conflicts reshaped the global cyber threat landscape.

title: Everything we launched during Agents Week
partialText: Our latest Agents Week has come to a close. Here’s a recap of all the announcements we made from Wallets to Radar.
